experiment.title: CPU vs naive GPU vs tiled GPU

verification.metric: naive GPU: max over n of (max rel. error) / (√n·u)
verification.reference: float64 product of 16 sampled rows at n = 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024

verification.metric: tiled GPU: max over n of (max rel. error) / (√n·u)
verification.reference: float64 product of 16 sampled rows at n = 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024

verification.metric: CPU baseline: max over n of (max rel. error) / (√n·u)
verification.reference: float64 product of 16 sampled rows at n = 64, 128, 256, 512

verification.metric: naive vs tiled: max over n of max |naive − tiled| / |C| / (√n·u)
verification.reference: the two GPU kernels on the same inputs (same summation order: expected 0 without FMA differences)

interpretation.claim: naive GPU: time grows like n³
interpretation.predicted: log-log slope 3 (2n³ flops; ±0.15 for cache effects)
interpretation.measured: 0.73 (no interval from 2 points) over n = 512 … 1024
interpretation.note: Fitted over the sizes whose median GPU (timestamp) time is at least 1 ms (n = 512 … 1024); smaller products are launch-, latency- or timer-bound, so their times do not grow like n³ yet. Over all 5 sizes the slope is 1.86. At least 3 sizes are needed for an uncertainty; with fewer, this claim stays undecided.

interpretation.claim: tiled GPU: time grows like n³
interpretation.predicted: log-log slope 3 (2n³ flops; ±0.15 for cache effects)
interpretation.measured: 1 size(s) with median ≥ 1 ms
interpretation.note: Fitted over the sizes whose median GPU (timestamp) time is at least 1 ms (n = 1024 … 1024); smaller products are launch-, latency- or timer-bound, so their times do not grow like n³ yet. Over all 4 sizes the slope is 1.64. At least 3 sizes are needed for an uncertainty; with fewer, this claim stays undecided.

interpretation.claim: CPU (blocked JS): time grows like n³
interpretation.predicted: log-log slope 3 (2n³ flops; ±0.15 for cache effects)
interpretation.note: Fitted over the sizes whose median time is at least 1 ms (n = 128 … 512); smaller products are launch-, latency- or timer-bound, so their times do not grow like n³ yet. Over all 4 sizes the slope is 2.55.

interpretation.claim: Tiling speeds the GPU kernel up
interpretation.predicted: tiled faster (speedup > 1): 16× fewer global loads (arithmetic intensity 4 vs 0.25 flop/byte); typically 2–10× on real GPUs
interpretation.note: The range is conservative (naive q1 / tiled q3 … naive q3 / tiled q1); undecided when it contains 1. The tiled kernel also reads A and B along rows (coalesced) where the naive one reads A across rows, so part of the gain is access pattern, not only reuse. On a software GPU workgroup memory is ordinary memory and barriers are expensive, so tiling can lose.

interpretation.claim: The naive kernel is bound by memory traffic, not arithmetic
interpretation.predicted: naive GFLOPS ≤ 0.25 × the bandwidth that serves its loads (8 bytes per multiply-add); tiled ≤ 4 × bandwidth
interpretation.measured: naive: 1524 GB/s of loads, tiled: 210 GB/s of global loads, at n = 1024
interpretation.note: Compare with your GPU's memory bandwidth (not known to the page). If the naive figure exceeds it, caches are serving most of its loads: the reuse happens, but in cache rather than in workgroup memory, and cache bandwidth is the limit.

interpretation.claim: The GPU beats one CPU core from some n on
interpretation.predicted: yes: GPU time is ≈ a fixed launch cost until the GPU is full, CPU time grows like n³ from the start (CPU measured up to n = 512)
interpretation.measured: GPU faster from n = 128 on; at n = 512: tiled GPU 0.393 (0.393–0.393) ms vs CPU 109.8 (109.5–111.6) ms
interpretation.note: Kernel time only; with upload and readback the tiled GPU takes 2.100 ms (wall). Where the crossover falls depends on the GPU, the CPU and the browser; undecided when the spreads overlap.

interpretation.claim: Median force error vs θ (log-log slope)
interpretation.predicted: 2: error ∝ θ² (the quadrupole term of a node's monopole about its center of mass, l/d ≤ θ); accepted 2 ± 0.25 for the θ³ term at large θ

interpretation.claim: Interactions per body vs θ (log-log slope)
interpretation.predicted: falls, exponent between −3 and 0: θ⁻³ cells per tree level in the large-N, uniform-density limit; flatter at these N, where the near field and the ~log N levels add a θ-independent part (CI, Plummer 4,096: −1.47)
interpretation.note: At θ = 1.2 each body does 173 interactions, 1% of brute force's 16,383.

interpretation.predicted: GPU median / replica median = 1 at every θ, within × / ÷ 1.7 (f32 arithmetic, tree-build order)
interpretation.measured: ratio 1.00 … 1.00 over 6 θ values
interpretation.note: Your GPU runs the same approximation as the reference; the trends above are the algorithm's, not the device's.

interpretation.claim: Brute-force time vs N (log-log slope, GPU ms)
interpretation.predicted: 2: N − 1 interactions for each of N bodies, O(N²) (± 0.1 for fixed costs)

interpretation.claim: Barnes-Hut time vs N (log-log slope, GPU ms)
interpretation.predicted: about N log N: 1.11 over N = 1,024 … 65,536; accepted 1.00 … 1.30, because interactions per body still grow faster than log N here
interpretation.note: Below 1: fixed costs (about 30 tree-build dispatches per evaluation) dominate over this whole range on this device, so the time barely grows with N.

interpretation.claim: Barnes-Hut interactions per body vs N (log-log slope)
interpretation.predicted: between 0 and 1: grows, but slower than brute force's N − 1 (→ log N for large N, 0.11 here; CI: 0.37)
interpretation.note: Deterministic counts (one distribution, one seed): the interval reflects curvature, not noise.

interpretation.claim: Crossover N (Barnes-Hut faster from here)
interpretation.predicted: exists: O(N²) overtakes O(N log N) at some N (CI, software GPU, wall ms: between 8,192 and 16,384)
interpretation.measured: between N = 8,192 and N = 16,384 (log-interpolated ≈ 14,800)
interpretation.note: Compared on GPU ms. Device-dependent: compare it with other devices, not with a fixed number. The interquartile ranges do not overlap at either point, so the bracket is resolved.

interpretation.claim: Tree-build share of Barnes-Hut GPU time vs N
interpretation.predicted: falls with N: the build is O(N) plus about 30 fixed dispatches, the traversal O(N log N)

experiment.title: Sorting N keys: bitonic, bitonic with workgroup memory, radix, CPU

verification.metric: bitonic (global): keys that differ from the CPU sort
verification.reference: Uint32Array.prototype.sort of the same keys, bit for bit: 42 sorts (warm-ups included) at N = 16,384 … 1,048,576

verification.metric: bitonic (workgroup memory): keys that differ from the CPU sort
verification.reference: Uint32Array.prototype.sort of the same keys, bit for bit: 42 sorts (warm-ups included) at N = 16,384 … 1,048,576

verification.metric: radix: keys that differ from the CPU sort
verification.reference: Uint32Array.prototype.sort of the same keys, bit for bit: 42 sorts (warm-ups included) at N = 16,384 … 1,048,576
u32 keys: no key map in this run

interpretation.claim: Bitonic sort (global): time vs N
interpretation.predicted: O(N log² N), the slope of N·log₂N(log₂N+1)/2: slope 1.15 over N = 131,072 … 1,048,576 (± 0.05)
interpretation.measured: slope 0.95 (95% CI 0.62 … 1.27, R² 0.987) from GPU-timestamp medians at 4 sizes
interpretation.note: Too noisy to decide: the 95% interval is wider than ± 0.2, enough to fit both O(N) and O(N log² N). Rerun, or run to a larger N.

interpretation.claim: Bitonic sort (workgroup memory): time vs N
interpretation.predicted: O(N log² N) compare-exchanges, global traffic N × dispatches: slope 1.15 … 1.26 over N = 131,072 … 1,048,576 (compute-bound … traffic-bound) (± 0.05)
interpretation.measured: slope 1.27 (95% CI 0.69 … 1.85, R² 0.978) from GPU-timestamp medians at 4 sizes
interpretation.note: Too noisy to decide: the 95% interval is wider than ± 0.2, enough to fit both O(N) and O(N log² N). Rerun, or run to a larger N.

interpretation.claim: Radix sort: time vs N
interpretation.measured: slope 1.05 (95% CI 0.37 … 1.73, R² 0.956) from GPU-timestamp medians at 4 sizes
interpretation.note: Too noisy to decide: the 95% interval is wider than ± 0.2, enough to fit both O(N) and O(N log² N). Rerun, or run to a larger N.

interpretation.claim: CPU sort (TypedArray.prototype.sort): time vs N
interpretation.predicted: O(N log N), the slope of N·log₂N: slope 1.08 over N = 131,072 … 1,048,576 (± 0.05)
interpretation.measured: slope 1.03 (95% CI 1.02 … 1.04, R² 1.000) from wall-clock medians at 4 sizes
interpretation.note: Within the interval: time grows like the operation count over this range.

interpretation.claim: Crossover: bitonic (global) (wall) becomes faster than the CPU sort
interpretation.predicted: device-dependent, no universal N; "none in range" is a valid outcome
interpretation.note: GPU wall time is submit → done of the sort alone (no upload or readback); a GPU is "faster" at an N only when its q3 is below the CPU sort's q1. In CI, on a CPU-emulated GPU, there is no crossover. Your GPU, driver, browser and CPU all move this point.

interpretation.claim: Crossover: bitonic (workgroup memory) (wall) becomes faster than the CPU sort
interpretation.predicted: device-dependent, no universal N; "none in range" is a valid outcome
interpretation.measured: between N = 32,768 and 65,536 (spreads overlap at the lower one): bitonic (workgroup memory) 0.40 ms (0.40–0.40) vs CPU 0.40 ms (0.40–0.50) at N = 32,768; bitonic (workgroup memory) 0.50 ms (0.50–0.60) vs CPU 0.90 ms (0.90–1.00) at N = 65,536
interpretation.note: GPU wall time is submit → done of the sort alone (no upload or readback); a GPU is "faster" at an N only when its q3 is below the CPU sort's q1. In CI, on a CPU-emulated GPU, there is no crossover. Your GPU, driver, browser and CPU all move this point.

interpretation.claim: Crossover: radix (wall) becomes faster than the CPU sort
interpretation.predicted: device-dependent, no universal N; "none in range" is a valid outcome
interpretation.measured: between N = 32,768 and 65,536 (spreads overlap at the lower one): radix 0.40 ms (0.40–0.40) vs CPU 0.40 ms (0.40–0.50) at N = 32,768; radix 0.50 ms (0.50–0.50) vs CPU 0.90 ms (0.90–1.00) at N = 65,536
interpretation.note: GPU wall time is submit → done of the sort alone (no upload or readback); a GPU is "faster" at an N only when its q3 is below the CPU sort's q1. In CI, on a CPU-emulated GPU, there is no crossover. Your GPU, driver, browser and CPU all move this point.

interpretation.claim: Ranking at the largest N (N = 1,048,576, GPU timestamps)
interpretation.predicted: fastest first: radix < bitonic (workgroup memory) < bitonic (global), on a GPU with fast workgroup memory
interpretation.measured: radix 2.36 ms (2.16–2.49) < bitonic (global) 4.26 ms (3.54–4.39) < bitonic (workgroup memory) 4.78 ms (4.06–4.85)
interpretation.note: Each adjacent pair counts as decided only when the interquartile ranges do not overlap. On the CPU-emulated GPU in CI the order is inverted (global bitonic fastest, radix slowest): there barriers are expensive and workgroup memory is ordinary cache.
